No. The evidence shows tree-cover loss across about **81.3 hectares**, or **2.23%** of the 3,643.5-hectare property, in 2021—not the whole property. A further 37.3 hectares of loss occurred in patches smaller than 0.5 hectares and was not counted as an event.

Most of the mapped event area was classified as planted forest. Tree-cover loss does not by itself establish that the land was permanently cleared or explain what caused the loss.
